summary.headline: Rossell Techsys FY26 revenue rose 87% to INR485 crore and Q4 revenue hit INR142 crore (+62% YoY), but margins were weaker than guided.
summary.overview: Management reported record Q4 revenue of about INR142 crore (+62% YoY) with profit of about INR9.5 crore, and FY26 revenue of INR485 crore (+87%), PBT of INR28 crore (from INR10 crore) and EBITDA of INR66 crore (from INR38 crore). Margins were below the company's stated 17-22% range, which management attributed to qualification costs for new semiconductor and space customers, training, and automation investment. Management guided FY27 revenue growth similar to FY26 (about 80-90%), a 50:50 split between aerospace & defence and non-aerospace & defence, and margin improvement. A QIP of about 7-10% of market cap is planned, alongside leasing a 210,000 sq ft facility.

financial_highlights.change: about 15% stated for FY26 by Jayanth; FY27 improvement expected

segments.name: Aerospace & Defence
segments.commentary: Consistent on-time delivery; Boeing agreed to level-load future schedules. Boeing program: about INR75 crore executed in FY26, about INR70 crore left for FY27, weighted to the first two quarters. Strategic agreements for T-7 of about USD200 million; ramp-up expected in later part of FY27.

segments.name: Semiconductor
segments.commentary: Emerged as a key growth driver in FY26 after qualification in Q2; volumes ramped immediately. Management guides 300-400% revenue growth in FY27. Onboarding a new overseas semiconductor customer; products are wire harnesses only.

segments.name: Space
segments.commentary: Moved from qualification to volume production with first large production batches; landmark multi-year contract of about INR400 crore. Guides 300-400% growth in FY27. Customer is Amazon; onboarding additional space customers.

segments.name: Semiconductor and space combined
segments.commentary: Approximately 20% of FY26 revenue came from these two segments, per management.

segments.name: MRO
segments.commentary: DPL licence and AS9110 MRO certification received; marketing to existing and external customers in India and US, with revenue pickup expected in coming quarters. No revenue quantum disclosed.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: About 98% of revenue is export; about 80% of total revenue from North America, with diversification into Southeast Asia, Middle East and Europe.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth similar to FY26 (about 80-90%); management did not give an absolute revenue number, though it referenced prior INR1,300 crore two-year target.
FY27 revenue split of about 50% aerospace & defence and 50% non-aerospace & defence.
Margins to improve in FY27 on EBITDA and PBT; current-competency margins quoted at 17-22%, with MRO higher and electromechanical integrated systems (phase two, 2028-29) targeted at 21-30%.
Inventory coverage to fall from 7.67 months toward 4 months over time.
Commercial aerospace RFPs expected by Q2 FY27; semiconductor target of up to USD200 million revenue in 3-5 years.
capex_capacity: Leasing an additional facility of about 210,000 sq ft near existing operations instead of constructing a new one; space and semiconductor programs to migrate there, with revenue expected comparable to existing facility.
Fundraise (QIP) of about 7-10% of market cap, to be used for capacity expansion, operational infrastructure and working capital for scale.
Evaluating options to strengthen Rossell Techsys Inc. (US subsidiary, RTI) infrastructure; a US facility is being refurbished per a customer requirement.
Workforce grew from 680 to nearly 1,200 over two years.
demand_pricing: Total order bookings about INR715 crore of confirmed POs (roughly 50:50 aerospace & defence vs non-aerospace & defence); about INR570 crore received during FY26.
Strategic agreements of about INR3,000 crore, over and above the confirmed order book, mainly aerospace & defence; POs placed against them 6-12 months before delivery.
Bids of about INR4,500 crore submitted in FY26 across aerospace, defence, space and semiconductors.

Margin pressure attributed to qualification costs (first article inspections) for new customers; price escalation handled via back-to-back supplier contracts, EPA clauses (accepted by some customers), and advance payments for long-lead single-source items.

qa_highlights.question: Why have margins been sequentially weaker than guided?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited heavy investment in people, infrastructure, training and new-customer qualifications (FAIs) that do not yet yield revenue; it expects repeat orders to lift profitability later.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Boeing loss-making program be executed in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR75 crore was executed in FY26 and about INR70 crore remains for FY27, high in the first two quarters and low in the last two.

qa_highlights.question: How much is the balance sheet and debt pressure, and how will the QIP be used?
qa_highlights.answer: The aim is to cut inventory from 7.6 months toward 4 months; QIP proceeds target capacity expansion, operational infrastructure and working capital, sized at 7-10% of market cap.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PAT margin and when will cash flow turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: No PAT margin figure given; management said it depends on QIP timing. CFO Jayanth said cash flow improvement is expected in coming years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR3,000 crore strategic contract value in addition to the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management confirmed the INR3,000 crore strategic agreements are over and above the INR715 crore confirmed POs.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export/geography split?
qa_highlights.answer: About 98% of revenue is export, with about 80% from North America; diversifying into Southeast Asia, Middle East and Europe.

risks_watch: Margin delivery versus the stated 17-22% range; FY26 margins fell short and FY27 improvement depends on qualification completion and automation.
Working capital intensity: inventory coverage still 7.67 months; debt rising, and the QIP timing and size (7-10% of market cap) are not yet fixed.
Customer concentration: one large customer per segment in space and semiconductor; Boeing program is loss-making in FY26 with balance in FY27.
Commercial aerospace entry and MRO revenue are at early stage with no quantified numbers; RFPs expected by Q2 FY27.
Facility lease of 210,000 sq ft and US subsidiary expansion add execution and cost risk.
Management gave limited quantified guidance, with several answers deferred or unclear (T-7 ramp timing, PAT margin).
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, scale and pipeline (sky's the limit), but evasive or vague on margins, PAT, MRO sizing and QIP timing, and frequently deferred questions to colleagues.
key_quotes: Financial year '26 marks the beginning of a structurally higher growth trajectory.
I've always said the margins will be between 17% to 22%.
The idea is to keep reducing that moving forward and eventually be a 4 month inventory company.
So it's kind of a back-to-back agreement in some cases that we have from our customers to our suppliers.

adds.what: Leased additional facility of ~210,000 sq ft near existing operations (space and semiconductor programs to migrate there)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth similar to FY26 (~80-90%, reiterated ~87%), backed by INR715 crore confirmed order book, INR3,000 crore strategic agreements and a leased 210,000 sq ft facility, though no absolute revenue number is given and margins fell below the 17-22% range in FY26.
